title: A Review on Transportation 5.0: Advancing Sustainable Mobility through Intelligent Technology and Renewable Energy
content: Transportation 5.0, a more sophisticated transportation system focused on human-centered design and inclusivity, is defined by cutting-edge technologies combined with societal demands. Its vari-ous components, intelligent infrastructure, connected and autonomous vehicles, shared mobility services, green energy solutions, and data-driven systems, come together to form an efficient and sustainable transportation network to tackle modern urban challenges. However, this evolution of transportation is intended to improve accessibility by creating environmentally benign substitutes for traditional fuel-based mobility solutions, even in addressing traffic management and control issues. Consequently, to promote a synergy for sustainability, the diversified nature of its compo-nents ought to be efficiently and effectively managed. Thus, this study aims to reveal the in-volvement of predicting core components of transportation 5.0 in the sustainable transportation system through a systematic literature review. This study also contemplates the causal model un-der system dynamics modeling to address sustainable solutions and movement towards sustaina-bility in the context of transportation 5.0. From the review, besides the developed causal model, it is identified that in the sustainable transportation 5.0 system, every core component management secures reduced environmental impact while increasing passenger convenience and the overall efficiency and accessibility of the transport network, even more advancing for developing nations. As the variety of transportation options, even focusing on electric vehicles, are successfully inte-grated, this evolution will eventually enable shared mobility, green infrastructure, and multimodal transit options.
